newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Focus on big spenders in new S.African budget.
newsitem.headline: Focus on big spenders in new S.African budget.

text.p: The South African government would focus on big spending government departments when it takes its first crack at multi-year budgeting, finance department director-general Maria Ramos said on Tuesday.
The departments were education, health, welfare, defence and the police, she told the parliamentary finance committee.
Ramos said that her department planned to finalise its first medium term expenditure framework (MTEF) this year.
"The MTEF will consist of rolling three-year budgets for each department and each province, which will be published as part of the 1998 budget," she said.
"These medium term plans will be determined within an envelope of what can be afforded and will reflect explicit considerations of policy priorities.
"They will give spending agencies a more stable framework within which to plan their expenditure, and a provide a baseline against which new policy initiatives can be assessed."
Meetings had already been held with the provinces to introduce them to the concept, which she admitted would require a complete change of attitude to budgeting by departments.
She hoped that by August/September the MTEFs from the provinces and national departments would be ready and that a consolidated MTEF would be ready by October/November.
This would then be presented to Cabinet and made available for discussion before being published with the next budget.
"So quite a lot of work and progress has been made on the actual implementation of the MTEF," she said.
"That will take us quite some way from the current system of budget and puts in place the disciplines that this committee has been requesting for some time," she said.
One area that would not be dealt with this year because of resource constraints would be the development of a multi year revenue framework, but this would be on the agenda next year.
Asked what she thought of plans by several government departments to introduce levies to supplement their budgets, Ramos said government had to be careful about how it introduced additional taxes.
Her department was studying the issue and would report to the cabinet soon.
